title: Sola fide does not make inward righteousness faith-only, nor deny other prerequisite acts
source_text: XXIX. Nec etiam, dum sic loquimur, affirmare volumus justitiam illam novam, quam Spiritus Sanctus in fidelibus creat, & a qua saepe in Scriptura justi sanctique nominantur, constare sola fide, non vero etiam charitate, caeterisque virtutibus, ad quas divinae gratiae beneficio formantur, & Christo conformes redduntur. Item neque per id negare intendimus, praeter fidei actum, multos alios a Deo praerequiri, & per gratiam ejus in nobis excitari, priusquam donemur illa justitia habituali, cujus respectu novi homines facti, & de novo ad Dei imaginem creati in Scriptura dicimur. Quales actus sunt timor judicii divini, peccati detestatio, serium vitae emendandae studium, pia nominis Dei invocatio, & si qui sint similes. Quin ultro quoque confitemur, justitiam illam semel nobis a Deo donatam, exercitio bonorum operum quotidie magis ac magis augeri atque increscere, Deumque illos, qui accepta gratia recte utuntur, bonis operibus sedulo vacantes, ampliori indies gratia ornare, atque cumulare; juxta illud Christi solenne promissum, Habenti dabitur.
pass_a_gloss: Nor, when we speak thus, do we wish to affirm that that new righteousness which the Holy Spirit creates in believers, and from which they are often named just and holy in Scripture, consists of faith alone and not also of charity and the other virtues by which they are formed by the benefit of divine grace and made conformed to Christ. Likewise we do not intend by that to deny that, besides the act of faith, many other acts are prerequisite by God and stirred in us by his grace before we are given that habitual righteousness with respect to which we are said in Scripture to have been made new people and created anew after God's image. Such acts are fear of divine judgment, detestation of sin, serious pursuit of amending life, pious invocation of God's name, and the like. Indeed we freely also confess that that righteousness once given us by God is daily more and more increased and grows by the exercise of good works, and that God adorns and heaps with fuller grace day by day those who use received grace rightly and diligently occupy themselves with good works—according to Christ's solemn promise: To the one who has, it will be given.
pass_b_english: Inward Spirit-wrought righteousness is not faith alone—charity and virtues belong too.
Other repentant acts precede habitual renewal; grace grows by good works (Habenti dabitur).

lemmas.gloss: To the one who has, it will be given

choices.why: Sanctifying inward righteousness includes more than bare faith.
